newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares in tight range on low volume.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares in tight range on low volume.

text.p: Lithuania's bourse remained in the doldrums on Wednesday, with shares holding steady in light trade, dealers said.
The group A index edged up just a notch or 10.96 points to 2,674.55 in central market trade of 1.25 million litas.
The Lithuanian Sea Shipping Company was active for the second straight day, turning over 206,500 litas. Its share price rose from 8.75 litas to 9.00 litas.
Rokiskis Cheese's price fell slightly, edging down to 49.01 litas from 49.50 litas, in trade of 223,000 litas.
The banking sector remained quiet, turning over 97,000 litas. Market leader Vilnius Bank's preference share price fell by 9.82 percent to 1,470 litas from 1,630 litas in trade of 11,760 litas.
"It is often quiet after a boom period. We had our bull run in January and maybe things rose too fast, too high," one dealer said.
He added that there was concern among some foreign investors about the future stability of the litas, but that those concerns should subside as the governmnet's plans become clear.
"Concern over the litas has had a big impact on T-bills but it has also had some impact on equities," the dealer said.
The government says it will eventually scrap the currency board under which the litas is pegged to the dollar at a four to one rate but says it will do nothing hasty.
The central bank says the peg will be in place until 1999.
Block trades of just 214,000 litas were made while volume on the secondary T-bill market reached only 112,000 litas.
